object.title: The awesome conjecture for coefficients of the logarithmic expansion
object.statement:
Let $z_i\geq2$ be positive integers, and define

$$
F=\sum_{s\geq0}\frac{a_s(r,j)}{n^s}+\sum_i c_i j(j-1)\cdots(j-z_i+1)\frac{1}{n^{z_i}r^{z_i}}\sum_{s\geq0}\frac{a_s(r,j-z_i)}{n^s}.
$$

For coefficient extraction, $[j^k n^{-h}]$ denotes the coefficient of $j^k n^{-h}$.

**The awesome conjecture.**

$$
[j^k n^{-h}]\,\ln(F)=0,\qquad k\geq h+2,
$$

and

$$
[j^{h+1}n^{-h}]\,\ln(F)=\frac{1}{(h+1)h}\left(\frac{1}{r^h}-2\right).
$$

The source identifies this as an earlier conjecture and contrasts it with a weaker theorem proved in the paper. Its general status is not resolved by the supplied text.
object.source_name: Paul Federbush, “A PROOF of Weak Graph Positivity, for a Large Range of the Parameters”, arXiv:2012.10927 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.10927

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).
